correctness.rationale: A row-stochastic matrix preserves constants, so in path-difference coordinates its induced ℓ¹ norm is the maximum variation of a unit cut indicator. At that cut, symmetry identifies the two cross blocks as transposes, and the admissible cross block is exactly the sub-stochastic edge-weight polytope of the cut's bipartite bandwidth graph: all unallocated mass can be put on the diagonal. Integrality and convexity thus give an optimal matching without assuming all symmetric stochastic matrices are mixtures of involutions. For p left hole runs and q right island runs, the two internal transition counts are at most 2p−e_L and 2q−e_R, where e_L,e_R are the adjacent switch indicators. The cut transition is 1 if those indicators agree and 0 otherwise, giving the two bounds used in the proof, even at finite endpoints. At even bandwidth 2k, the only way to exceed 4k−1 is with both adjacent sites unchanged and k runs on each side. That forces every switched depth to be 2,4,…,2k; the depth-2k hole has no permissible partner. At odd bandwidth 2k−1 the run counts alone suffice. Set s=min(n,4k), m=ceil(s/2). The parity target has exactly m ones and the sorted transpositions have constant displacement at most 2ceil(s/4)−1 on every nonempty matching (check s modulo four); if s<n the last alternating entry is zero, so there is no extra endpoint jump. This realizes min(n−1,4k−1), including n=2 or r≥n−1. Symmetry really matters: the bandwidth-two permutation with row images (0,3,1,4,2,5) maps the cut at 3 to (1,0,1,0,1,0), of variation 5 rather than the symmetric maximum 3. An independently written sweep of all banded involutions using an adjacent-edge cut histogram passed for 52 (n,r) pairs, 21,330 involution instances; separate deduplication by cut confirmed the reported 1,373 profiles across the original 30 pairs.
residual_risks: The finite check corroborates the theorem, not a proof covering all dimensions. The norm is for the open, unweighted path, not cyclic variation or for only PSD stochastic filters.

value.rationale: For a local conservative filter, the exact worst amplification is a stability bound on arbitrary path data. The tradeoff between locality and oscillation is not captured by stochasticity alone: positivity and symmetry still allow amplification, but symmetry removes two potential transitions at even bandwidth. The parity plateau and the sharp finite-size cutoff tell precisely when enlarging the stencil cannot worsen that bound, and the explicit local swaps show it cannot be made smaller on this class.
residual_risks: No implication is asserted for any particular smoothing operator, strict-contraction subclass, or different graph.
